sources.name: GitHub issues of xsoh/moment-hijri
sources.version: GitHub REST API 2022-11-28, state as of 2026-11-11
sources.license: GitHub Terms of Service (user content; only facts and our own summaries are kept)

provenance.notes: URL, number, title, state, dates, counts and labels are copied from the API response of each issue. Category, components, summary, resolution and lesson are written by the researcher (tools/extract/field-reports/curation) after reading the issue body returned by the search API and, for the issues listed in docs/research/field-reports.md, the full thread. daysOpen of an open issue is measured to the retrieval date. fixedBy is filled mechanically from merged pull requests that name the issue after a closing keyword. Reports marked needs-review state a cause that the researcher inferred from the symptom without a confirming statement in the issue.

reports.title: Simply including moment-hijri into the project sets global locale for moment to ar-sa
reports.summary: Merely importing the plugin switched the host library's global locale to Saudi Arabic, because it registers its month names by updating — and thereby activating — a locale. Reported in 2018 and closed as not planned in 2025.
reports.lesson: Calendar support has no import-time side effects and no global locale state; calendar and locale are arguments.

reports.title: Format to iD/iM/iYYYY - gives arabic text not English
reports.summary: Formatting a Hijri date with numeric tokens produced Arabic text for a user who wanted Latin output, with no documented way to choose. Open for more than seven years.
reports.lesson: Calendar, language and numbering system are independent: a Hijri date can be formatted in English with Latin digits, or in Arabic with either digit set.

reports.title: Shawwal month not return from moment hijri (2022)
reports.summary: In 2022 the plugin returned Ramadan as the name of the current month when it was Shawwal, for that year only. Open since.
reports.lesson: Month boundaries come from the official Umm al-Qura table and are tested for every month of every covered year against a reference implementation (ICU islamic-umalqura).

reports.title: Hijri month lengths differ from official Umm al-Qura data in 760 entries, incl. an impossible 28-day month
reports.summary: The embedded Umm al-Qura month-length table disagrees with the official Saudi calendar in 760 of 1,740 entries for 1356–1500 AH and contains an impossible 28-day month.
reports.lesson: Our Hijri table is extracted by script from an authoritative source with provenance, validated (every month 29 or 30 days, year lengths 354 or 355), and cross-checked against ICU.
